key: Rouse thyself by thyself, examine thyself by thyself, thus self-protected and attentive wilt thou live happily, O Bhikshu!
s: Late in the chapter on the mendicant, the verse addresses him directly; the Theravāda commentary, Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā XXV.10, reads it as spoken for a former ploughman who admonished himself beneath the tree where his old rags hung whenever discontent came, and so became an arahat.
src: The Theravāda commentary, Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā XXV.10 (on verses 379 to 380), trans. Burlingame, Buddhist Legends, vol. 3 (1921)

opened.edition: E. W. Burlingame, Buddhist Legends, HOS 30 (1921), archive.org buddhistlegends03budd (OCR)
opened.locator: Story XXV.10 (Dhammapada 379 to 380), The Monk and the Ragged Garment, Norman pp. 115 to 116
notes on chapter XXV (none on 379 to 380)

evidence.words: the Elder caused him to take his loin-cloth and his plow and hang them up on the branch of a tree … whenever he became discontented, he would go to the foot of the tree and admonish himself. … After a few days he attained Arahatship. … My son has admonished himself by himself, and has thus reached the consummation of the religious life.
evidence.gloss: Story XXV.10: the new monk’s loin-cloth and plough were hung on a tree; whenever discontent came he went to its foot and admonished himself, and within days attained arahatship; answering the monks who said he lied, the Teacher says his son admonished himself by himself and so reached the goal of the religious life, and speaks verses 379 to 380. The Pali explanation agrees: attanāva attānaṃ codaya sāraya (urge and remind yourself by yourself).

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref and at match). Story XXV.10 read in full in the packet: the reading is the commentary’s. Corrected the wording: “praise of” became “spoken for” (the Teacher answers a charge of falsehood and states the monk’s attainment; praise is a slight overreach) and “rebuked his discontent” became “admonished himself ... whenever discontent came”, the story’s own self-by-self act; plain sense tightened to 45-word budget (“Late in the chapter”). Place and src unchanged. entry-check ok.
